title: Workday acquiring Portland agentic AI identity management startup
source_used: Workday press release on PR Newswire (The Business Journals page blocked, HTTP 403)
key_facts: Workday announced on 13 Oct 2026, at Workday Rising in Las Vegas, that it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire C1.ai, a "leading agentic identity platform for people and agents".
C1.ai connects to systems such as email, CRM, code repositories, finance systems and cloud infrastructure, giving each person and agent the right access and removing it when no longer needed.
The release cites C1.ai research that 95 percent of large US companies already run autonomous agents, and Deloitte research that only 21 percent have a mature way to govern them.
Workday says it would become the identity governance layer for people, money and agents; C1.ai builds on the Workday Agent System of Record.
Expected to close in Q4 of Workday's fiscal 2027 (ending 31 Jan 2027), subject to customary conditions; no price in the release.
Advisers: BofA Securities and Orrick for Workday; Qatalyst and Ashurst Perkins Coie for C1.ai.
Gerrit Kazmaier, president, product and technology at Workday, and Alex Bovee, CEO and co-founder of C1.ai, are quoted.
quote_evidence: C1.ai connects to the systems a business runs on – from email and CRM to code repositories, finance systems, and cloud infrastructure – giving each person and agent the right access at the right time and removing it the moment it's no longer needed.

The rapid adoption of AI agents has accelerated this challenge: C1.ai's research shows that 95% of large U.S. companies already run autonomous agents, yet according to Deloitte's State of AI research, only 21% report having a mature way to govern them.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of Workday's fiscal year 2027, ending January 31, 2027, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions.
why_it_matters_hint: Workday plans to manage access for AI agents as well as employees, but the benefits described are the company's own claims.
notes: The Business Journals (Portland) page blocked (HTTP 403); its headline places C1.ai in Portland, which the press release does not state. The release is Workday's own promotional text; benefit claims are attributed to it.
